name: Grimm 2020, Kerr-cat resonator, with a hypothetical bias during the ramp
question: If the squeezing drive of the Kerr-cat resonator were raised along its tanh ramp with a weak one-photon bias, which cat well would the resonator choose, and would the choice follow the linear-stage law or the balance of the two wells?
assumptions: Units: the amplitude damping rate kappa = 1/T1 = 1/15.5 us = 6.45e4 per second is 1; time in units of T1.
Kerr: K/2 pi = 6.7 MHz, so K = 653 kappa; the resonator is deep in the single-photon Kerr regime.

Squeezing drive: epsilon_2/2 pi = 17.5 MHz at the plateau, so eps2 = 2 epsilon_2 = 3510 kappa and the stored cat states hold epsilon_2/K = 2.6 photons; the drive follows a tanh profile over 320 ns = 0.0206/kappa, written as (1 + tanh(5(2s - 1)))/2 in the sweep variable s = t/(320 ns), since the paper states the shape and duration but not the width of the tanh; the width is chosen so that the drive starts below the threshold kappa/2 (eps2 = 0.16 kappa at s = 0).
Thermal occupation of the resonator n_th = 0.04 (the paper's value), entering the loss as kappa n_th D[a†].

The bias is hypothetical: the paper prepares the wells by the parity of a Fock state and applies the one-photon drive only after the ramp; here a one-photon drive h = 50 kappa (below the paper's cat-Rabi drives of 72 to 633 kappa) is kept on during the ramp to ask which well a bias would select.
The ramp is fast against the loss, kappa/sqrt(r) of order 1e-3, so the seed is the preparation (the closed limit of the law), and slow against 1/2K as the paper requires.
Truncation at 24 quanta for cat states of 2.6 photons; the hold of 0.1/kappa (1.5 us) keeps the drive on after the ramp.

provenance.reference: A. Grimm et al., Stabilization and operation of a Kerr-cat qubit, Nature 584, 205 (2020), arXiv:1907.12131v2: K/2 pi = 6.7 MHz, T1 = 15.5 us, epsilon_2/2 pi = 15.5 to 18 MHz, n_th = 0.04, tanh ramp over 320 ns (main text and Section VII, Table 2)
